Okay guys here's my essay:

Nostalgia, the Psychological Time Machine to Simpler Times

Nostalgia is an incredibly strong feeling as it is rooted in the memories and emotions of simpler times, giving adults a chance to escape the stresses of their responsibilities. Nostalgia is a connection back to childhood, reminding us of the times when we had the freedom to live without a care in the world Not only does nostalgia provide immense comfort, it also greatly impacts cognitive development as a child. We learn problem-solving skills, creativity, balance, and even decision making. All of these things build the foundation that later translates into our skills we use as an adult. Subconsciously, we think about those childhood toys that were there for us in the past--the toys that shaped our personalities. Nostalgia is an incredible coping mechanism. While unfavorable childhood experiences may correlate with avoidance coping strategies, favorable childhood memories correlate positively with adaptive coping strategies (Batcho K. I. (2013)). Nostalgia reminds us of who we are and how our identity developed over time. We do, however, tend to distort these memories. Even if one's childhood was less than ideal, we can focus on the tangible items that did bring us joy, even if it was all we had. We also experience the pain of abandoning these toys. They sit unused, alone with nothing but dust and cobwebs. We feel some sadness thinking about how these toys that helped us grow are now retired. The bitter feeling of being unable to go back, realizing how it can never be the same again. This concept brings physiological discomfort to us, because it's something that is out of our control. All we have are our memories, and those memories can provide some sort of catharsis when encountering major life changes during present times. Additionally, nostalgia--both favorable and painful--serves as an incredible bonding experience between a group. Reminiscing on shared or similar childhood experiences strengthens friendship, though this only tends to work for those born within the same generation. Regardless, people don't dismiss others' nostalgia; if anything, they begin to reminisce on their own memories, even if they aren't shared. Nostalgia can form and strengthen bonds between people. If we had a time machine, most people would choose to revisit our childhood. Not necessarily to change some embarrassing moment, but to simply experience that joy we can't have anymore. Childhood wonder only exists during one's childhood. We yearn for that magic. It's ironic, as children we long to grow up, yet as adults we wish we could be kids again. Remember those toys that brought you into the world of imagination. Think about that rocking horse that you once believed was a real horse carrying you through across the country. Reminisce on the things that soothed you, taught you balance, and brought you into a whole new world. Enjoy the feeling of nostalgia. You are strong. You are brave. You can do it. Your past toys are cheering for you. References
-# Batcho K. I. (2013). Nostalgia: retreat or support in difficult times?. The American journal of psychology, 126(3), 355–367. https://doi.org/10.5406/amerjpsyc.126.3.0355 -# Bennett, M. (2025, May 10). Unlocking childhood memories with nostalgic toys benefits. The Parenting Pro. https://theparentingpro.com/unlocking-childhood-memories-with-nostalgic-toys-benefits/ -# Batcho , K. I. (2014, May 6). Nostalgia: A mental time machine. Psychology Today. https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/longing-for-nostalgia/201405/nostalgia-a-mental-time-machine -# Batcho, K. (n.d.). Speaking of Psychology: Does nostalgia have a psychological purpose? With Krystine Batcho, PhD. American Psychological Association. https://www.apa.org/news/podcasts/speaking-of-psychology/nostalgia
 (edited)
